summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration file that sets up a development container for Quarto documentation work. It defines a service called 'quarto-doc-base' that builds a Docker image from a local Dockerfile, configures it with various build arguments and volumes for development, and keeps it running indefinitely so developers can work inside it.

explanations.2: This tells the spell-checker to ignore the word 'tinytex' since it's a legitimate tool name that wouldn't be in a standard dictionary.
explanations.6: This specifies which Docker image to use or create; 'latest' means we want the most recent version of this image.
explanations.15: USER_UID and USER_GID are numeric identifiers for the user account inside the container; 1000 is a common default for the first non-root user, though this gets overridden by VS Code's settings.
explanations.18: These are feature flags (true/false settings) passed to the Dockerfile during build to control what optional software gets installed in the container.
explanations.22: Starting the container as root gives it elevated privileges, which is sometimes needed for development tools but is generally less secure than using a regular user.
explanations.27: This mounts the parent directory of the compose file into /workspace inside the container with read-write access, so code changes on your computer are immediately visible in the container.
explanations.28: This persists your bash command history across container restarts by storing it in a local file instead of losing it when the container stops.
explanations.29: This gives the container access to Docker's control socket, allowing you to run Docker commands from inside the container (Docker-in-Docker).
explanations.31: The ${HOME} syntax substitutes your actual home directory path at runtime, so it points to wherever your user's home folder actually is on your machine.
explanations.39: This command runs an infinite loop that never exits, which keeps the container alive and ready for you to connect to it and work interactively.
